newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dozens injured as Mexico eviction turns violent.
newsitem.headline: Dozens injured as Mexico eviction turns violent.

text.p: Dozens of people were injured and four arrested on Wednesday when police battled more than 200 families trying to resist eviction near the Mexican beach resort of Acapulco, witnesses said.

The clash took place at around 0930 am (1430 GMT) when about 100 police armed with riot gear arrived at the settlement, on the edge of Punta Diamentes in southwestern Guerrero state, to evict 232 families from land they were allegedly occupying illegally.

Processo Gonzalez Calleja, a local deputy and member of the leftwing Party of the Democratic Revolution, was knocked unconscious and taken to hospital with severe head injuries after trying to intervene with police.
A PRD statement received late on Monday said four people had been detained and dozens hurt in the violence, which took place about 9 miles (15 km) from the glitzy Acapulco resort.
Police demolished the houses in the attack.
Police said the families had been occupying the land for two months, but PRD representatives said they had been living there for six years.
